say: Builder works best with the superpowers plugin, which adds planning, TDD and review skills.
why: It gives every task a plan, a test and a review step.
how: /plugin marketplace add obra/superpowers-marketplace, then /plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace

say: Builder pairs well with gstack, a set of skills for browsing, QA and shipping.
why: It adds a real browser and ship workflows that builder can route to.

say: The GitHub CLI is not signed in, so builder cannot read issues or pull requests for you.
why: Intake and review need a signed-in gh.

say: Your git commits are not signed, and builder asks for signed commits.
why: A signed commit shows that you, and not someone else, made it.
how: Use SSH signing. On macOS, use a Secure Enclave SSH agent (for example the open-source Secretive app) and create the key there with "notify" protection, so agents can sign without you. Otherwise run `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_signing` and keep the passphrase in the OS keychain or agent. Then run `git config --global gpg.format ssh`, `git config --global user.signingkey <path-or-key>`, `git config --global commit.gpgsign true` and `git config --global tag.gpgsign true`. Last, register the public key on GitHub as a signing key: `gh auth refresh -h github.com -s admin:ssh_signing_key`, then `gh ssh-key add <key.pub> --type signing`.

say: Builder has no channel to reach you when a long task finishes.
why: A channel lets builder send you a short note instead of waiting in a terminal.
how: Ask me: "set up reach" (the reach skill walks you through it).

say: You run several Claude sessions at once, and matchblox can show them together with their usage.
why: It lists live sessions and limits in one view.

say: You have three or more live sessions, so builder can help you run them as a fleet.
why: Parallel sessions need one owner per task to avoid clashes.

say: Your weekly usage is at 80% or more, so builder can help you plan the rest of the week.
why: A budget stops one big task from using the whole limit.

say: This project has no written canon, so builder cannot tell your rules from its own guesses.
why: A short canon (DESIGN.md or docs/canon/) gives every session the same rules.
